boundaries: the text a reader sees in place of a stored message
what each surface shows when the text cannot be recovered
the seam between needsDecryption and decryptForDisplay
the reader's key pair, loaded per message or per page

prior_ledgers_read: 0a4bb3a71 -- the immediately preceding review, of G3b. Its findings were all of one shape: a path that showed or sent something it should have refused. That shape is what this review followed into the display surfaces.
9803e5f57 -- fe-silent-429: a refusal that reached nobody. Consulted because the display rule's failure statuses decide what each caller shows.
7c62d192b -- no findings recorded; consulted for prior work on these pages.
notes: The commit under review claimed the rule lived in six places. It lived in eight. The count came from memory rather than from a sweep, and was wrong twice before a mechanical enumeration settled it.

Twice during this review I navigated these files with line numbers that my own edits had already invalidated, because deleting the extracted hooks shifted every line below them. Both times the read landed on unrelated code. Every later edit was anchored on unique text instead.
Commit 6767ec885 was made while one test was red. The run reported one failure and one error and I committed without reading it. Corrected forward in 23698daae rather than amended away.

instruments.evidence: G3c-0 replaced five implementations of the display rule with one shared function plus a hook, across MessagesPage, ExpandedMessage and SearchResultsPage. The boundary crossed is what a reader sees in place of a stored message.
Read 0a4bb3a71, 9803e5f57 and 7c62d192b before starting. The first is this review's own predecessor and named the shape to follow.
Deferred to the differential, which is the artifact for a refactor: not one payload, but the same inputs through both implementations.
The artifact here is the rendered text per surface. The differential printed it for eight message shapes across four key and decryption states.

instruments.why: No handler changed; this is client-side display only.

instruments.evidence: The status values are one union in one module; no caller spells them independently.
Checked what each of the five callers receives. They disagree about failure, which is why the result carries a status rather than only text.

The instrument that found both defects. Ran the five old implementations and the new shared one over eight message shapes crossed with keys present or absent and decryption succeeding or throwing, and diffed what each call site would display. Reading the diff had found neither.
The new optional ownKeys parameter crosses a seam: undefined means load them, null means there are none. Both batch callers pass the resolved value, so null is never mistaken for absent.
Each control breaks the reader, not the writer: reverting the guard makes the status wrong, and reverting the key memo makes the loader run again.
The differential's fixtures were the message shapes production stores, including the one that mattered: an own message held only as the copy wrapped for the recipient.
Ordinary plaintext, v1 and v2 messages all still display; the suites for every consuming page pass.
The inputs that must not display as text -- unreadable own copies, failed decryption -- now report failure rather than handing back the blob.
Empty ciphertext, a version string nobody recognises, and a prefix without a matching version were all exercised.
The search results page was the sibling that proved the others wrong: it alone tested the v2: prefix for an own message, which is the check the extraction had dropped.
No branch became unreachable; the early return for an unreadable own copy is reached by a real stored message.
Every failure reaches a caller that decides what to show. None is swallowed.
Found the second defect: the old search page hoisted one getOwnKeys call above its loop, and the extraction put it inside, once per message and twice per mod mail message.
The point of the change: one rule instead of five.
Swept for both shapes. Deferred the surface sweep to pass 2, which is where it found what pass 1 had missed.

instruments.evidence: Nothing is written; a failure leaves the surface showing its own choice of fallback.

findings.summary: An own message held only as the copy wrapped for the recipient came back as not-encrypted, so every surface showed the raw blob as though it were the message. This device cannot open that copy; the extraction had adopted the hole from the five copies that had it, while the search results page was the one place that got it right by testing the v2: prefix.

control.observed: AssertionError: expected 'not-encrypted' to be 'failed' -- the rule reports the blob as ordinary text.

findings.summary: getOwnKeys was called once per message, and twice for a mod mail message. It caches nothing: each call opens IndexedDB and imports a key. The search results page had loaded them once above its loop, and the extraction made that one load per result.

control.observed: AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times.

findings.summary: CompactPostCard's feed preview was a seventh copy of the rule, testing encryption_version === 'v1' alone with no v2 and no prefix check, so every v2 message rendered as raw ciphertext in the feed. It also carried the own-message hole, loaded keys twice per card in a list, and painted the ciphertext before attempting to decrypt. Neither it nor its only renderer had any test.

PinnedMessagesBar did not decrypt at all. It returned encrypted_content truncated to eighty characters, as the row text and as the title attribute, so every pinned encrypted message showed its ciphertext. The first control for this fix PASSED when replayed, which is its own finding: every message in that suite was plaintext, where the old and new code agree, so nothing there could see the defect.

control.observed: Rebuilt after the blind control was fixed in efc3405b6. AssertionError: expected '1 pinned messagev2:secret-blob-nobody...' not to contain 'secret-blob'.

findings.summary: ModMailConversationPage was an eighth copy, with the same narrow 'v1' test, the same own-message hole and the same two key loads per message. Its suite asserted only that a body element existed, so nothing there could have noticed.

control.observed: AssertionError: expected 'modMailConversationPage.actions.backT...' to contain 'the real mod mail text'. The page renders and the decrypted text is absent, rather than the container being empty.

findings.summary: Making the pinned bar decrypt would have made its text asynchronous for every message, including messages that were never encrypted, which breaks the synchronous assertions in its suite and delays text that needs no keys. A pure predicate was needed so a surface can paint such text on the first render instead of after a round trip.

control.observed: AssertionError: expected false to be true -- the narrowed predicate misjudges v2 and prefixed messages.
